nodes.title: Laptop hardware components
nodes.description: Install and configure RAM, storage, wireless cards, ZIF connectors, battery, display, and CPU thermal components in laptop systems.

nodes.title: Mobile device display components
nodes.description: Compare and contrast display components, mobile connectivity types (Bluetooth, NFC, Wi-Fi), and mobile device synchronization methods.

nodes.title: Configure mobile device accessories
nodes.description: Set up and configure accessories, ports, and features of mobile devices including enterprise mobility management tools.

nodes.title: TCP/UDP ports and protocols
nodes.description: Compare and contrast TCP vs UDP, common port numbers (HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, SSH 22, FTP 21, DNS 53), and their application purposes.

nodes.title: Common networking hardware
nodes.description: Compare and contrast routers, switches, access points, firewalls, patch panels, PoE injectors, and their roles in network infrastructure.

nodes.title: Wireless networking protocols
nodes.description: Compare 802.11 standards (a/b/g/n/ac/ax), 2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz frequency bands, encryption types, and channel configuration.

nodes.title: Networked host services
nodes.description: Summarize services provided by networked hosts: DHCP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, file servers, print servers, and authentication services.

nodes.title: SOHO network configuration
nodes.description: Install and configure a basic wired/wireless SOHO network with proper IP addressing, NAT, DHCP, and firewall rules.

nodes.title: Internet connection types
nodes.description: Compare and contrast DSL, cable, fiber, cellular (4G/5G), satellite, and WiMAX internet connection types and their characteristics.

nodes.title: Network types and features
nodes.description: Compare and contrast LAN, WAN, MAN, PAN, WLAN, and their topology characteristics and use cases.

nodes.title: Cable types and connectors
nodes.description: Identify and explain cable types (USB, HDMI, DisplayPort, Ethernet, SATA, Thunderbolt) and the purpose of each connector type.

nodes.title: Connector and port types
nodes.description: Compare USB generations (USB-A, USB-C, USB 3.x), video connectors (VGA, DVI, HDMI, DP), and storage interface types.

nodes.title: RAM installation
nodes.description: Install the appropriate RAM type (DDR4/DDR5), form factor (DIMM/SO-DIMM), capacity, and configure dual-channel memory.

nodes.title: Motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards
nodes.description: Install and configure motherboards, CPUs (socket types, cooling), and expansion cards (GPU, NIC, sound card) in desktop systems.

nodes.title: CPU and motherboard features
nodes.description: Configure BIOS/UEFI settings, understand CPU socket compatibility, PCIe slots, and form factors (ATX, Micro-ATX, ITX).

nodes.title: Storage device installation
nodes.description: Select and install HDDs, SSDs (SATA/NVMe/M.2), optical drives, and configure RAID levels (0, 1, 5, 10) for appropriate use cases.

nodes.title: Power supply installation
nodes.description: Install and replace power supplies with proper wattage, connector types (24-pin, EPS, PCIe), and 80 Plus efficiency ratings.

nodes.title: Display installation and configuration
nodes.description: Configure displays with appropriate resolution, refresh rate, panel type (IPS/VA/TN), and connector (HDMI, DisplayPort, VGA, DVI).

nodes.title: Printer deployment and configuration
nodes.description: Deploy and configure multifunction devices including laser, inkjet, and thermal printers with network connectivity and print queue setup.

nodes.title: Printer consumables replacement
nodes.description: Install and replace printer consumables: ink cartridges, toner cartridges, fuser assemblies, drum units, and maintenance kits.

nodes.title: Cloud computing concepts
nodes.description: Summarize cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), deployment types (public, private, hybrid, community), and cloud characteristics.

nodes.title: Client-side virtualization
nodes.description: Summarize hypervisor types (Type 1 bare-metal, Type 2 hosted), VM resource requirements, snapshots, and virtual network configurations.

nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology
nodes.description: Apply the CompTIA 7-step troubleshooting process: identify the problem, establish a theory, test the theory, plan a solution, implement it, verify, and document.

nodes.title: IT foundations and support
nodes.description: Understand the IT technician role, safety procedures, basic computer components, and professional communication with customers.

nodes.title: Storage drive troubleshooting
nodes.description: Diagnose and resolve issues with HDDs (clicking, bad sectors), SSDs, RAID array degradation, and boot drive failures.

nodes.title: Display and video troubleshooting
nodes.description: Troubleshoot no signal, dead pixels, incorrect resolution, screen flickering, projector problems, and GPU-related display issues.

nodes.title: Hardware component troubleshooting
nodes.description: Diagnose POST errors, beep codes, RAM failures, CPU overheating, and power supply issues in desktop and laptop systems.

nodes.title: Network troubleshooting
nodes.description: Diagnose no connectivity, limited connectivity, intermittent issues, and slow network speeds using ping, ipconfig, tracert, and nslookup.

nodes.title: Wireless network troubleshooting
nodes.description: Troubleshoot wired and wireless network issues including APIPA addresses, DNS failures, authentication errors, and signal interference.

nodes.title: Windows editions
nodes.description: Identify Windows 10/11 Home, Pro, Enterprise, and Education editions, their feature differences, upgrade paths, and licensing requirements.

nodes.title: OS installation and upgrades
nodes.description: Perform Windows OS installations, in-place upgrades, and clean installs while managing partition types, file systems, and boot options.

nodes.title: Windows command-line tools
nodes.description: Use Microsoft command-line tools: ipconfig, ping, tracert, netstat, nslookup, sfc, chkdsk, DISM, and PowerShell commands.

nodes.title: Windows features and tools
nodes.description: Use Windows OS features including Task Manager, Device Manager, Registry Editor, System Restore, and MMC snap-ins.

nodes.title: Windows settings
nodes.description: Configure Windows settings for display, power, updates, accessibility, and system properties using both Settings app and Control Panel.

nodes.title: Windows networking and command line
nodes.description: Configure Windows network adapters, wireless profiles, VPN connections, and use command-line networking tools for diagnostics.

nodes.title: Application installation and management
nodes.description: Install, configure, and manage applications including compatibility settings, virtual app delivery, and application troubleshooting.

nodes.title: macOS features and tools
nodes.description: Identify common macOS features (Finder, iCloud, Time Machine, Spotlight) and basic shell commands in Terminal.

nodes.title: Linux client OS tools
nodes.description: Use basic Linux commands (ls, pwd, grep, chmod, sudo), understand distributions, package managers (apt/yum), and file permissions.

nodes.title: Cloud-based productivity tools
nodes.description: Identify and configure cloud-based productivity platforms (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace) and collaboration features.

nodes.title: Physical and logical security measures
nodes.description: Summarize physical security controls (door locks, cameras, badge readers) and logical controls (ACLs, MFA, principle of least privilege).

nodes.title: Wireless security protocols
nodes.description: Compare WPA2 (TKIP/AES) and WPA3, enterprise vs personal authentication, RADIUS, and wireless security best practices.

nodes.title: Social engineering attacks
nodes.description: Explain phishing, vishing, smishing, tailgating, shoulder surfing, dumpster diving, and impersonation attacks and prevention strategies.

nodes.title: Malware types and threats
nodes.description: Identify malware types (virus, worm, Trojan, ransomware, spyware, keylogger, rootkit) and common attack vectors.

nodes.title: Malware detection and removal
nodes.description: Detect, remove, and prevent malware using anti-malware tools, scanning techniques, quarantine, and safe mode removal procedures.

nodes.title: SOHO network security
nodes.description: Configure SOHO network security: change default credentials, enable WPA3, set up DMZ, configure firewall rules, and guest networks.

nodes.title: Windows security configuration
nodes.description: Configure Windows Defender Firewall, BitLocker encryption, UAC, security policies, and browser security settings.

nodes.title: Workstation security hardening
nodes.description: Apply workstation security best practices: strong passwords, screen locks, patch management, least privilege, and disable unused ports/services.

nodes.title: Mobile and data security
nodes.description: Secure mobile and embedded devices with screen locks, remote wipe, MDM enrollment, full-device encryption, and proper data disposal methods.

nodes.title: Windows OS troubleshooting
nodes.description: Troubleshoot Blue Screen of Death (BSoD), slow startup, application crashes, update failures, and use Windows Recovery Environment tools.

nodes.title: PC security issue troubleshooting
nodes.description: Diagnose malware infection symptoms, account lockouts, unauthorized access attempts, browser redirects, and suspicious network activity.

nodes.title: Mobile OS and application issues
nodes.description: Troubleshoot mobile OS problems including app crashes, slow performance, battery drain, connectivity issues, and screen problems.

nodes.title: Documentation best practices
nodes.description: Create and maintain IT documentation: network diagrams, knowledge bases, SOP manuals, asset inventory, and incident reports.

nodes.title: Change management practices
nodes.description: Implement change management: submit requests, obtain approvals, create rollback plans, update documentation, and communicate changes.

nodes.title: Backup and recovery methods
nodes.description: Implement workstation backup strategies: full, incremental, differential backups; 3-2-1 backup rule; and test recovery procedures.

nodes.title: Safety procedures
nodes.description: Use common IT safety procedures: ESD prevention (anti-static straps), electrical safety, proper lifting, and fire suppression systems.

nodes.title: Environmental impacts and controls
nodes.description: Summarize environmental controls: temperature, humidity, power protection (UPS, surge protectors), and proper equipment disposal regulations.

nodes.title: Privacy, licensing, and policy
nodes.description: Explain PII protection requirements, software licensing (EULA, open-source, commercial), data retention policies, and regulatory compliance.

nodes.title: Communication and professionalism
nodes.description: Apply professional communication skills: set expectations, avoid jargon, follow up with customers, and document completed work properly.
